title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — Mock Exam #1

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #1
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. In which part do you find the seeds of a mango? (1 mark)
   A. Root
   B. Stem
   C. Fruit
   D. Leaf

2. The touch-me-not plant folds its leaves when touched. This shows that plants can (1 mark)
   A. lay eggs
   B. respond to changes
   C. move from place to place
   D. eat food

3. Which of these is a stem that stores food and is eaten or used for sugar? (1 mark)
   A. Sukuma wiki leaf
   B. Sugarcane
   C. Tomato
   D. Bean pod

4. Which of these is a mammal that lives in water? (1 mark)
   A. Crocodile
   B. Whale
   C. Tilapia
   D. Frog

5. Which of these animals is a reptile? (1 mark)
   A. Butterfly
   B. Tilapia
   C. Lizard
   D. Hen

6. Which activity shows that air takes up space? (1 mark)
   A. Singing a song
   B. Lighting a candle
   C. Shining a torch
   D. Blowing up a balloon

7. A kilogram of stones and a kilogram of feathers have the same (1 mark)
   A. Mass
   B. Shape
   C. Volume
   D. Colour

8. Which of these is a solid? (1 mark)
   A. Air
   B. Steam
   C. A stone
   D. Milk

9. Which of these is a correct grouping? (1 mark)
   A. Air, stone and salt are gases
   B. Milk, water and juice are liquids
   C. Steam, oil and rice are gases
   D. Chalk, water and steam are solids

10. What does a football need to keep its shape? (1 mark)
   A. Sand
   B. Air
   C. Milk
   D. Water

11. Which is the best way to manage the food remains from the school kitchen? (1 mark)
   A. Put them in a compost pit
   B. Bury plastic with them
   C. Burn them near classrooms
   D. Throw them in a river

12. Which of these is non-decomposable waste? (1 mark)
   A. Leaves
   B. Banana peel
   C. Tin can
   D. Egg shells

13. What can leak from old batteries and pollute soil and water? (1 mark)
   A. Milk
   B. Harmful chemicals
   C. Clean water
   D. Sweet juice

14. Which is an example of reducing waste? (1 mark)
   A. Leaving litter at a picnic
   B. Burning plastic
   C. Carrying a cloth shopping bag
   D. Throwing a bottle in a river

15. Which of these is an example of reusing water? (1 mark)
   A. Buying bottled water
   B. Using water from washing vegetables to water plants
   C. Leaving taps open
   D. Pouring water down the drain

16. Which of these is NOT a way to conserve water? (1 mark)
   A. Washing dishes under a running tap
   B. Using a basin
   C. Fixing leaks
   D. Harvesting rainwater

17. Which of these is a pull? (1 mark)
   A. Closing a door by pushing
   B. Opening a drawer by its handle
   C. Kicking a ball
   D. Pressing a bell

18. Which of these holds objects together? (1 mark)
   A. Glue
   B. A smooth floor
   C. Oil
   D. A rolling ball

19. Which force makes it hard to push a heavy box along a rough floor? (1 mark)
   A. Friction
   B. Light
   C. Sound
   D. Colour

20. A ball is rolling and you kick it in the direction it moves. What happens? (1 mark)
   A. It gets smaller
   B. It changes into a solid
   C. It speeds up
   D. It stops

21. What should you do when doing force experiments? (1 mark)
   A. Throw heavy things
   B. Run with sharp tools
   C. Keep fingers away from moving parts
   D. Push others

22. A flat sheet of paper falls slower than a stone because (1 mark)
   A. Air pushes up on the flat paper more
   B. The stone is bigger
   C. Paper is bigger
   D. Gravity does not pull paper

23. Why are tyres made with rough patterns? (1 mark)
   A. To grip the road
   B. To make them shiny
   C. To reduce friction
   D. To make them lighter

24. Which of these uses of light is for plants? (1 mark)
   A. Making roots taller
   B. Making their own food
   C. Making them bend downward
   D. Making them cold

25. Which of these is a torch used for? (1 mark)
   A. To cool a room
   B. To give light in the dark
   C. To make sound
   D. To make food

26. What happens to light when it hits an opaque object? (1 mark)
   A. It becomes heat only
   B. It is blocked
   C. It passes through completely
   D. It becomes sound

27. Which of these is translucent? (1 mark)
   A. Wood
   B. Clear glass
   C. Tissue paper
   D. Stone

28. Which use of heat helps farmers to store maize? (1 mark)
   A. Colouring paper
   B. Drying grain
   C. Writing
   D. Making shadows

29. Which of these is unsafe? (1 mark)
   A. Switching off an iron
   B. Asking an adult to light a fire
   C. Playing with matches
   D. Using gloves

30. Which of these is a safety rule when cooking? (1 mark)
   A. Leave children alone at the cooker
   B. Turn pot handles inwards
   C. Turn handles outwards
   D. Touch the hot pot

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Describe how you would measure 300 ml of water using a measuring jug, and how you would measure the mass of a mango. (5 marks)

32. State two uses of light. (2 marks)

33. Explain why sand is not a liquid although it can be poured. (3 marks)

34. A block is pulled along a rough floor and along a smooth floor with the same force. Describe and explain what you would see. (4 marks)

35. A pupil wants to find out which material is transparent, translucent or opaque. Describe a test. (4 marks)

36. A pupil says that empty containers have nothing inside. Explain why the pupil is wrong and how you would show it. (5 marks)

37. Describe how waste attracts pests that harm health. (3 marks)

38. Name the two forces studied in this topic. (2 marks)

39. Explain why a translucent roof sheet is useful in a classroom during the day. (3 marks)

40. Give two symptoms of an unhealthy digestive system. (2 marks)

41. Describe what you would put in a portfolio about vertebrates and invertebrates. (4 marks)

42. Describe the differences between mammals and birds. (4 marks)

43. Explain how animals show the signs of life: feeding, growing, and reproducing. Give an example of each. (4 marks)

44. Give three examples where a force holds objects together. (3 marks)

45. Name the three main sources of heat. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #1 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — Fruit
   Seeds are found inside fruits.

2. B — respond to changes
   Folding when touched is a response to a change in the surroundings.

3. B — Sugarcane
   Sugarcane stems store sugar.

4. B — Whale
   A whale breathes air and feeds milk to its calf, so it is a mammal even though it lives in water.

5. C — Lizard
   A lizard has dry scaly skin.

6. D — Blowing up a balloon
   The balloon swells because air takes up space inside.

7. A — Mass
   Both are 1 kg. The feathers take up much more space.

8. C — A stone
   A stone keeps its shape.

9. B — Milk, water and juice are liquids
   Milk, water and juice are all liquids.

10. B — Air
   The air inside fills the football.

11. A — Put them in a compost pit
   Kitchen waste can be composted.

12. C — Tin can
   Metal does not rot easily.

13. B — Harmful chemicals
   Old batteries have harmful chemicals.

14. C — Carrying a cloth shopping bag
   A reusable bag means fewer plastic bags are thrown away.

15. B — Using water from washing vegetables to water plants
   Using water twice is reusing.

16. A — Washing dishes under a running tap
   A running tap wastes water.

17. B — Opening a drawer by its handle
   A handle is pulled toward you.

18. A — Glue
   Glue, nails and ropes use forces to hold things together.

19. A — Friction
   Rough floor gives large friction.

20. C — It speeds up
   A force in the direction of movement increases speed.

21. C — Keep fingers away from moving parts
   Safe practice prevents injuries.

22. A — Air pushes up on the flat paper more
   Air pushes up more on the wide flat sheet.

23. A — To grip the road
   Grip needs friction.

24. B — Making their own food
   Plants use light to make food.

25. B — To give light in the dark
   A torch is an artificial light source.

26. B — It is blocked
   Opaque objects do not let light pass.

27. C — Tissue paper
   Tissue paper lets some light through.

28. B — Drying grain
   Heat dries wet things.

29. C — Playing with matches
   Matches can start fires.

30. B — Turn pot handles inwards
   Handles turned inwards cannot be knocked easily.

SECTION B
----
31. (5 marks)
   Answer: Place the jug on a flat surface, pour water until the level reaches the 300 mark with your eye level with the water. For the mango, place it on a balance and read the mass in grams.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for flat surface, pouring to 300 ml, eye level, using a balance, reading in grams.

32. (2 marks)
   Answer: To see, for safety, to discourage pests, for plants to make food, to dry clothes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: Each grain of sand is a small solid with its own shape. The grains are piled together and pour as a pile.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for grains being solids, 1 mark for grains having shape, 1 mark for conclusion.

34. (4 marks)
   Answer: The block moves slower or a shorter distance on the rough floor. Rough floors give more friction.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four points.

35. (4 marks)
   Answer: Use a torch in a dark room. Put tissue paper, clear plastic and a book one at a time between the torch and a wall. Record whether all, some or no light passes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for equipment, 1 mark for method, 1 mark for observation, 1 mark for classification.

36. (5 marks)
   Answer: They are full of air which is matter. Air takes up space. For example the upside-down cup pushed into water stays dry inside or a balloon swells with air.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for air inside, 1 mark for air is matter, 1 mark for an activity, 1 mark for the observation, 1 mark for the conclusion.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: Rotting waste attracts flies, rats and cockroaches. They spread germs to food and cause diseases such as diarrhoea and cholera.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for pests, 1 mark for germs, 1 mark for diseases.

38. (2 marks)
   Answer: Gravity and friction.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: It lets daylight in, so lamps are not needed, saving electricity and money.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for daylight, 1 mark for no lamps, 1 mark for saving.

40. (2 marks)
   Answer: Stomach ache, bloating, diarrhoea, vomiting, constipation, worms (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

41. (4 marks)
   Answer: A drawing of each animal, its name, whether it is a vertebrate or invertebrate, one sign of life seen, put together in a folder.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four items.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: Mammals have hair or fur and feed their young on milk and most give birth to live young. Birds have feathers and wings and lay eggs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four differences.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: Feeding: a goat eats grass. Growing: a chick becomes a hen. Reproducing: a hen lays eggs, or a cow gives birth.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sign with example, plus 1 mark for explaining growth as getting bigger.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Glue holding paper, nails holding wood, rope tying things, stitches holding cloth, screws.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: The sun, fire and electricity.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two and 2 marks for all three.
